title: Playback, correction and validation
objective: Decide whether a workflow with disputed permissions needs a playback.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: A playback reviews the maps with the customer before they reach the executive. Use it when it resolves a specific uncertainty. Don't add one by default.
Glean's Blueprint process pairs DITL interviews with a playback. A playback is worth its time when:

items: The future state can't be responsibly finalized live.
Several teams need to agree on the same workflow.
A targeted demonstration can resolve a specific question, such as whether permissions behave as expected.

blocks.x: Show the current and proposed work side by side. Call out the assumptions. Demonstrate only the prioritized tasks needed to test the hypothesis. Ask directly: "What is wrong or missing?" Record the customer's corrections in the log, with the date and who made them.
A playback is not a required extra meeting in every deal. Each playback or demo should have a defined question, an owner, and a decision date. If it doesn't, it's a delay, not validation.
A playback is for correction. Show the map, ask what's wrong, and record every change.

blocks.title: The playback loop
blocks.alt: A three-step loop: show the mapped workflow to the people who do the work, collect corrections, and update the map and log, then repeat until the owners confirm it.

items.label: Show the map
